body.statement:
After matching the common selector-gated syntax,
\[
\Theta_H=\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^+)\cap
\left\{\theta:\operatorname{supp}_{p_\theta}(S)=H,\ p_\theta(c)>0\text{ for every }c\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)\right\}
\subseteq\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^+).
\]
The inclusion is strict whenever the published class contains a law violating at least one displayed restriction.  Moreover, \(\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}\subseteq\Theta_H^2\subseteq\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^+)^2\).  If a pair in \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{LGS}}^{(5)}\) assigns positive mass outside \(H\), has a zero admissible cell, or fails equality on some coordinate of \(O_H\), then that pair is not in \(\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}\).  Consequently the published failure relation alone does not imply membership in the fixed-support global-twin relation; if it contains any such pair, \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{LGS}}^{(5)}\not\subseteq\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}\).
body.justification: This inclusion comparison isolates the logical obstruction to importing a larger-class branchwise witness into the fixed-support completeness theorem.
body.gap: Theorem 5 of Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser certifies specified failure constructions in its published model, but it does not type every output as an exact-\(H\), full-joint-law twin in the restricted-support interior subclass.
body.consumer: Reviewers and implementers can distinguish a legal fixed-support nonidentification certificate from a witness that silently adds a context or preserves only part of the supplied joint table.
body.proof_tex:
By definition, \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^+)\) imposes the common recursive selector-gated syntax before the two present restrictions are imposed.  The definition of \(\Theta_H\) adds exactly
\[
\operatorname{supp}_{p_\theta}(S)=H
\quad\text{and}\quad
p_\theta(c)>0\ \text{for all }c\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+).
\]
This proves the displayed set equality and inclusion.  If the published class contains a law violating either restriction, that law belongs to the right-hand class but not \(\Theta_H\), proving strictness.

The first predicate in the definition of \(\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}\) is membership of both coordinates in \(\Theta_H\).  Therefore
\[
\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}\subseteq\Theta_H^2
\subseteq\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^+)^2.
\]
Now take a pair in \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{LGS}}^{(5)}\).  Positive mass outside \(H\) violates exact-support membership in \(\Theta_H\); a zero admissible cell violates its interior condition; and failure of equality on any coordinate of \(O_H\) violates the defining all-cell equality of \(\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}\).  In each case the pair is outside \(\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}\).  Thus existence of even one such pair proves noninclusion.  Without an existence premise, the fact that the published definition omits these predicates cannot by itself prove set noninclusion, which is the logical correction made in the proposed statement.
